chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not leave four rak'at after Maghrib, whether in travel or in residence, and my father did not leave thirteen rak'at at night, whether in travel or in residence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of voluntary rak'at to pray after Maghrib according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt’s devotional practices, linking Imam al-Sadiq’s specific instruction on post-Maghrib nafl prayers to the established tradition of his father, Imam al-Baqir. The emphasis on praying thirteen rak'at both in travel (*safar*) and residence (*hadr*) highlights the principle that voluntary night prayers are not merely expedient shortcuts during journeys but integral components of a consistent spiritual routine, reflecting the Prophetic model of *Qiyam al-Layl*.
